name: @zipir/mcp

tools.name: list_formats
tools.description:
List video formats (call this before create_lesson when the user names a style)

Use when someone asks which styles exist, or before create_lesson if they said a style ("short", "explainer", "vertical"). Returns format ids to pass to create_lesson; never hard-code an id, read it here. No minutes are spent.

tools.name: list_voices
tools.description:
List narrator voices (call this before create_lesson when the user names a voice, a tone or a gender)

Use when someone asks which voices exist, wants a female or male narrator, a calm or lively tone, or English narration. Returns each voice with its name, a one-sentence tone, language (tr or en), gender, accent, tier and a short audio sample. Pass a voice `key` to create_lesson. Optional `language` narrows the list. Premium voices spend 1.5x minutes. No minutes are spent here.

language.description: Only voices that speak this language.

tools.name: list_lessons
tools.description:
List this account's recent lessons (use when someone asks "my videos", "what did I make", or wants to continue an earlier one)

Use when the user refers to their own earlier work: their videos, the lesson they started yesterday, the one waiting for approval. Returns the newest lessons with id, title, status, minutes and a link to open each. Read-only and free. Pass `status` to narrow (queued | rendering | done | failed) and `limit` (default 20, max 50).

tools.name: create_lesson
tools.description:
Create a narrated video lesson from a document, text or web page (use when someone wants a document turned into a training, safety or procedure video)

Use when the user brings a document, a block of text or a web page and wants a video, a lesson, an explainer or a summary video of it. Accepted sources: a file (PDF, DOCX, PPTX, MD or TXT, max 50 MB) sent as multipart, which the local MCP server takes as `file_path`; plain `text` (max 5 MB); or a public http(s) `url` whose readable text becomes the document. Every on-screen sentence cites the source paragraph it came from, so use this when the user needs traceable training, safety or procedure videos. Narration is Turkish. Returns a lesson id immediately; nothing renders and no minutes are spent until approve_lesson. Follow it with get_lesson until the storyboard needs approval. With an Idempotency-Key the same request inside 24h returns the same lesson (same key, different body is 409). API documentation: https://zipirapp.com/en/api/

text.description: The lesson text itself (UTF-8, max 5 MB).

url.description: A public http(s) page; its readable text becomes the document.

format.description: Video format. GET /v1/formats lists the live set.

lang.description: Language of the video's narration and on-screen text. Omit it and an English document gets an English video, any other document a Turkish one. A document in another language than the one you ask for is translated: the quoted source stays in its own language, the narration is in the requested language.

voice.description: Narrator voice key from GET /v1/voices. A voice that declares a language (the premium ones) also sets `lang`; a `lang` that differs is a 400 voice_lang_mismatch. The standard voices declare none and leave `lang` alone. Omit it for the default voice. Premium voices use 1.5x minutes: a 60 s video spends 90 s.

file_path.description: Path to a local file on this machine (PDF, DOCX, PPTX, MD, TXT; max 50 MB).

tools.name: get_lesson
tools.description:
Check a lesson's status (poll this after create_lesson and after approve_lesson)

Use whenever you need to know where a lesson stands: after creating it, while it renders, or before downloading. `status` is the machine state (queued | rendering | done | failed), `phase` is finer, `needs_approval` is true while the storyboard waits for a human, and `next` says which call to make next. Costs no minutes.

tools.name: approve_lesson
tools.description:
Approve the storyboard and start rendering (the only call that spends the account's minutes)

Use only after the user has seen the storyboard and agreed: this is the panel's approval button. The minutes for the lesson are held at this call and the render is queued. Do not approve on the user's behalf without their go-ahead. Check get_usage first if the balance may be tight.

tools.name: edit_lesson
tools.description:
Change one scene of a lesson (rewrite, shorten, retitle or restyle it); no render starts

The panel's own frame edit reached with an API key: the system proposes a patch to one scene and the source-quote check still decides -- a sentence the document does not support is refused. Name the target with scene_index or cue_index, exactly one of them (a cue is a scene's caption, so it names that scene). The call starts no render; the change is prepared in the background and accepting it stays the owner's step in the panel. Nothing is charged here: minutes are held when the video is rendered again (rerender).

scene_index.description: 0-based position of the scene in the storyboard. Exactly one of scene_index / cue_index.

cue_index.description: 0-based position of the spoken caption; a caption belongs to a scene, so it names that scene. Exactly one of scene_index / cue_index.

operation.description: rewrite: say it again in the document's own words. shorten: the same point in fewer words. retitle: a new scene title. style: change how the scene looks, not what it says.

instruction.description: What exactly should change, in one or two sentences. The source check still applies: the document must support the new sentence.

tools.name: rerender
tools.description:
Render a finished lesson again (the minutes rule is the approval's own)

Draws the lesson's current approved storyboard again: same scenes, new video. Only a lesson whose status is done can be rendered again; an accepted edit leaves the lesson in that state, so re-rendering after an edit is this call. Minutes are treated exactly as at approval: a lesson already charged for its length holds nothing new, and the account's limits and the key's own cap still apply. The live video keeps serving until the new one lands. This call can spend minutes: confirm with the owner first.

tools.name: get_download
tools.description:
Get a signed download link for the finished video (use when the video is ready and the user wants the file)

Use once get_lesson says the video is done. Returns a URL (valid 900 s) to the MP4, not the file itself: hand the link to the user or fetch it. `variant=720` is the light copy every plan gets, `variant=1080` is full quality and needs a paid plan.

tools.name: get_usage
tools.description:
Check remaining video minutes before spending any (call this before approve_lesson if unsure)

Use when the user asks how much is left, or before approve_lesson when the balance may be tight. `remaining` is what this key can spend now: the account's own balance as the billing page shows it (plan minutes left plus bought packs, or the free trial plus packs), narrowed by the key's own monthly cap if it has one; never a second rule. `used` is this key's minutes in the current period (finished videos plus minutes held for its lessons still rendering); `limit` = used + remaining. approve_lesson answers 402 quota_exceeded when the lesson does not fit.
